Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

variable adjective

changeable

also changeable, varying, inconstant, variable weather, unsettled

classical

Cic. N.D. 3.30
Liv. 2.7: animus vulgī (Lewis & Short)

mūtābilis, mūtābile

declension

changeable, liable to change

The plain word for what can change or keeps changing.

Other words

  • varius, varia, varium — changing, varying; various

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 135, 136: changing, shifting (wind, weather); Traupman 289

    Its everyday senses are “various, of different kinds” and, of colour, “mottled, many-coloured” (varius porcus); of a thing that changes, “changeable” (Lewis & Short). It fits where English says “varied” or “mixed”; for what changes over time mūtābilis is clearer.

  • inconstāns, inconstantis — changeable, fickle, unsettled

    declension · also used · classical · Plin. NH 18.352: ventī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 10.16: litterae (Lewis & Short)

    Of people, fickle or inconsistent; of winds and weather, unsettled.

  • variābilis, variābile — changeable

    declension · also used · late Latin · Apul. Mund. (Lewis & Short)

    Post-classical and rare (Lewis & Short); the classical words above are better.

Examples

  • omne igitur corpus mūtābile est

    so every body is liable to changeCic. N.D. 3.30

See also variable, change.
